answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before entering auctions, then answer random liveness and consistency challenges; failing one burns the bond and removes its accumulated reputation. Because rewards and voting weight accrue to a bonded identity over time, an attacker cannot cheaply split one honest history into thousands of fresh agents: every fake pays a separate bond and transaction fees, while coordinated failures expose the cluster. The ledger can call these bonds opal, copper, and kernel tiers, but scarcity is what matters.
